corrected_proposal.disposition: Replaced the unsupported claim of an all-program February rollback with a documented, narrower action: temporary withholding notices for 22 Title X grants issued March 31, effective April 1, 2025. The broader ACA-repeal and all-support claims remain unverified.
corrected_proposal.title: Administration Temporarily Withholds 22 Title X Grants
corrected_proposal.description_short: On March 31, 2025, Title X grantees were notified that the administration would temporarily withhold funding for 22 grants beginning April 1.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: On March 31, 2025, 16 Title X grantees received notices that the Trump administration was temporarily withholding funds for 22 fiscal year 2025 grants, effective April 1. Title X supports family-planning care, including contraception. The Guttmacher Institute estimated that if the withholding became permanent, at least 834,000 people could lose access to Title X-funded care over a year; that figure is conditional, not a count of confirmed losses.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On March 31, 2025, 16 Title X grantees received notices that the administration would temporarily withhold funding from 22 fiscal year 2025 grants beginning April 1. The Guttmacher Institute reported that all 13 direct grants to Planned Parenthood affiliates were included. Title X supports family-planning care, including contraceptive services. Guttmacher estimated that at least 834,000 people could lose access to Title X-funded care over a year if the withholding became permanent; that is a conditional projection, not a count of people already deprived of services. The action targeted specified grants and did not end all federal family-planning funding or rescind the Affordable Care Act’s contraceptive coverage requirement. The available sources do not quantify how many patients lost care while funds were withheld or establish when the affected funds were restored. The notices and estimate do not identify individual patients or prove that a specific clinic closed.
organization_tags: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

impact_proposal.confidence_reason: The notices and temporary funding action are documented; the largest cited access effect is a conditional estimate if withholding became permanent.
impact_proposal.rationale: The administration temporarily withheld a portion of Title X grants, and the notices covered 16 grantees and 22 grants. The conditional access estimate supports a material potential harm and reach, but the record establishes no institutional damage, procedural abuse, or private gain; those dimensions are 0. The withholding was temporary, with duration and restoration unresolved, so persistence remains limited.
impact_proposal.basis: Sixteen grantees were notified of temporary withholding for 22 FY2025 grants effective April 1; Guttmacher estimated potential effects if the withholding became permanent.
impact_proposal.notes: Weighted total 2.70, recomputed from the six impact-v2 dimensions. Editorial estimate only.

proposed_survivor_patch.title: Trump’s Inaugural Committee Paid His Washington Hotel for Event Space, Rooms and Meals
proposed_survivor_patch.description_short: The inaugural committee paid Trump’s Washington hotel for rooms, meals and event space during the January 2017 inauguration.
proposed_survivor_patch.description_medium: During the January 2017 inauguration, the 58th Presidential Inaugural Committee booked rooms, meals and event space at Trump International Hotel in Washington. WNYC and ProPublica reported internal emails and receipts documenting payments and a dispute over event-space pricing. The report said the final rental price was unclear.
proposed_survivor_patch.description_long: During the January 2017 inauguration, the 58th Presidential Inaugural Committee booked rooms, meals and event space at Trump International Hotel in Washington. In December 2018, WNYC and ProPublica reported on interviews, internal emails and receipts documenting the committee’s payments to the Trump Organization and a dispute over event-space pricing. The hotel’s managing director offered $175,000 per day for ballroom and meeting-room use, or $700,000 for four days. An inaugural planner questioned the proposed rates, and the article said it was unclear what amount the committee ultimately paid for the rental. This evidence documents a commercial relationship and a pricing concern; it does not establish the Trump Organization’s net profit, a hundreds-of-thousands amount earned during inauguration weekend, or a final determination that the prices violated law. A separate D.C. attorney general complaint filed in 2020 alleged overpayment for event space, but its allegations belong to a later lawsuit record and are not proof of the frozen row’s weekend-profit claim. The event description should remain limited to payments and price negotiations documented in the reporting.
